title: binornd

gpu_support.notes: Sampling currently runs on the host RNG path; GPU parameters use an owning-provider gather-and-reupload fallback so output remains resident with matching floating precision.

description: `binornd(n,p)` generates binomial random samples for positive integer trial counts `n` and success probabilities `p`. Size-vector and dimension-list forms are supported.
behaviors: MATLAB-compatible `n` and `p` inputs are `single` or `double`; `n` contains positive integers and `p` contains values in `[0,1]`.

Typed-integer `n` and `p` are independent all-eight-class extensions in `runmat` compatibility mode; values remain authoritative until the explicit binary64 sampling boundary and reject when they are not exactly representable there.
`n` and `p` support scalar expansion and matching array shapes.
Without explicit size arguments, the output shape is the scalar-expanded parameter shape.
With explicit size arguments, nonscalar parameters must match the requested shape.
MATLAB-compatible size controls are integer-valued `single` or `double`; all eight typed-integer classes are accepted as exact structural controls in `runmat` compatibility mode.
A single size value produces a square matrix, any nonpositive dimension produces an empty array, and trailing singleton dimensions beyond the second are ignored.
The output is `single` when `n` or `p` is single and is otherwise `double`; a resident input produces a resident result on the first resident input's owning provider.

faqs.question: Can n be fractional?
faqs.answer: No. RunMat requires `n` to be a positive integer trial count.

faqs.question: Does a typed-integer size change the output class?
faqs.answer: No. Size arguments are structural controls; output precision is selected by `n` and `p`.
